topic: The mount force-claim design leaves open
canonical_claim: The mount force-claim design leaves open whether a forced mount should also refuse to start the GC scheduler, so that a diagnostic tool taking ownership cannot also start reclaiming; the stated decision ("mounts as WRITE") argues no, while the blast radius of a diagnostic tool triggering GC argues yes.

topic: The isContentAddressed() whole-part transaction contract
canonical_claim: The isContentAddressed() whole-part transaction guard is duplicated across six MergeTree files, so a future caller that omits it could silently corrupt a CAS part. D2 (definitely duplicated): the projection whole-part-transaction guard `if (!isContentAddressed()) begin/commitTransaction()` is copy-pasted across six files (`MergeTask` x3, `MutateTask`, `MergeProjectionPartsTask`, `MergeTreeDataWriter`, `IMergeTreeDataPart`); forgetting it in a new call site is a silent-corruption class, tracked as issue B58.; Borrowed projection storage shares the parent whole-part transaction: `DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::beginTransaction` and `commitTransaction` must be no-ops when `has_shared_transaction` is true. A borrowed projection transaction makes `beginTransaction` and `commitTransaction` no-ops, with the parent transaction passed from `src/Storages/MergeTree/DataPartStorageOnDiskFull.cpp:41` and the no-op behavior implemented at lines 347 and 363. Projection build, merge, and mutation call sites can always invoke `beginTransaction` and `commitTransaction`; the storage decides whether it owns the transaction. Projection tasks may call `commitTransaction` unconditionally because a borrowed CAS projection rides the parent transaction and its `commitTransaction` is a no-op. The borrowed-projection transaction rule removes six duplicated `if (!isContentAddressed()) begin/commitTransaction()` guards from merge and mutate paths; the two sites that decide whether a projection borrows the parent transaction remain unchanged.; Projection sub-parts must use the parent part's whole-part transaction; commit `24f89d7ce78` routed merge/mutate projection sub-parts through that parent transaction, and commit `73b03c9a1e4` encapsulated the rule in borrowed projection storage. Additionally, `DataPartStorage` owns the rule for whether a projection storage opens its own transaction or borrows the parent transaction, so call sites do not need storage-specific transaction branches. Additionally, A logical clone of a part should be one operation represented by one disk transaction rather than independent autocommit file operations, especially for object-storage-like disks. Additionally, CAS cannot use early sub-part commits as a read-back mechanism because publishing a sub-part before its parent would expose a partial part; the sub-part must borrow the parent transaction and read staged files through its overlay. Additionally, `DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::beginTransaction` and `commitTransaction` are no-ops when `has_shared_transaction` is true, centralizing the rule that CA projections ride the parent whole-part transaction. Additionally, `getProjectionPartBuilder` sets `use_parent_transaction = !is_temp_projection || isContentAddressed()` so a CAS temporary projection sub-part shares the parent whole-part transaction. Additionally, `MergeTask` uses a `projection_uses_parent_transaction` flag and unconditional projection `beginTransaction`/`commitTransaction` calls so CAS projection sub-parts share the parent whole-part transaction.

topic: ContentAddressedTransaction::unlinkFile deliberately no-ops for committed content
canonical_claim: ContentAddressedTransaction::unlinkFile deliberately no-ops for committed content files; a future caller that expects surgical committed-file deletion would silently retain the bytes.; Risk register #4 (Medium, confirmed): `ContentAddressedTransaction.cpp:1294-1336`'s `unlinkFile` case 3 is a deliberate fail-open no-op for unlinking a committed content file (load-bearing for MergeTree's file-by-file removal pattern, tracked as B123); any future caller that surgically deletes one committed file without a whole-part `removeDirectory` would silently keep the bytes. Suggested action: pin the MergeTree invariant with an assertion/flag or a dedicated test.

topic: Cross-namespace RENAME TABLE is non-atomic and
canonical_claim: Cross-namespace RENAME TABLE is non-atomic and can leave a table split across namespaces after a mid-loop exception; the operation is idempotent and re-drivable.

topic: B171 is protected by contract
canonical_claim: B171 is protected by a durable build-root `+1` edge for adopted blobs and a fail-closed commit path that aborts when the dependency closure cannot be proven. A durable precommit edge must make an adopter's build root structurally reachable before adoption, and commit must re-check the whole closure and fail closed on absence; each half is independently necessary.; Build-root reachability and fail-closed commit are both required to prevent the `B140` dangle; either mechanism alone still has a counterexample.

topic: B151 requires a freshly contract
canonical_claim: B151 requires a freshly written part's final ref to publish at lock-free tmp-to-final `moveDirectory`, with rollback dropping the early-published ref when the transaction is abandoned. For a staged tmp-to-final part move, `ContentAddressedTransaction::moveDirectory` only re-keys the transaction view and does not call `publishStaging`; durable ref operations occur at commit.

topic: B59 occurred because projection temp blobs
canonical_claim: B59 occurred because projection temp blobs were recorded in an open transaction without a committed ref, so committed-only `resolveRef` returned `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` during read-back.

topic: P6 was a suspected S09 mutation
canonical_claim: P6 was a suspected S09 mutation carry-forward failure: the failing run had 2876 MiB pool growth and 34.5% S3 write errors versus 1.4 MiB and 12.5% on the passing rerun, leaving open whether write failure caused a full re-upload.

topic: The non-Atomic part-path parser contract
canonical_claim: The non-Atomic part-path parser can anchor `data/<db>/<table>/detached/<part>/...` on the inner part-shaped component, producing a spurious table namespace that `DROP TABLE` never cleans. For an Ordinary database, detached part paths can be parsed into a sibling namespace instead of the table namespace, leaving refs and blobs that `DROP TABLE` never cleans up. For non-Atomic paths, `findPartDirComponent` must anchor on the first reserved `detached` component before scanning right-to-left for a part-shaped component, so detached paths fold into the table namespace with `part_name == detached`.; Task A5's detached-part-path fix anchors the reserved `detached` directory component left-to-right (first match), not the right-to-left scan the original spec sketched, because a right-to-left scan would incorrectly anchor on the inner part-dir-shaped component first.

topic: MOVE PART or MOVE PARTITION to
canonical_claim: MOVE PART or MOVE PARTITION to a CA disk was architecturally unimplemented: `PartPathParser::findPartDirComponent` had no `MergeTreeData::MOVING_DIR_NAME` case, so files under `moving` resolved to the same literal ref `moving`.

topic: The deeper MOVE-to-CA failure was that
canonical_claim: The deeper MOVE-to-CA failure was that non-zero-copy `clonePart` used per-file `copyFile` with a fresh autocommit transaction for each file, so a whole part could not publish as one CAS manifest and the second file collided on ref `moving`.

topic: During the outage, Keeper committed the
canonical_claim: During the outage, Keeper committed the `block_id` znode and part-znode `all_1117_1117_0` even though the CA blobs and manifest did not durably reach paused RustFS and the committing replica was then killed.

topic: When RustFS is paused, uploadPendingBlobs in
canonical_claim: When RustFS is paused, `uploadPendingBlobs` in the post-Keeper `ContentAddressedTransaction::commit` hangs until the CAS budget and throws; the transaction destructor then rolls back the local part.

topic: The old ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::commitPart order contract
canonical_claim: The old `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::commitPart` order was `renameParts` → Keeper multi → `transaction.commit`, with part disk transactions committed only inside `transaction.commit` after the Keeper decision and under the `data_parts` lock. In the failing interleaving, `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::commitPart` builds Keeper ops, calls `transaction.renameParts()`, executes `tryMultiNoThrow(ops)` to commit block-id and part-znode, and only then calls `transaction.commit()` to upload blobs and publish the CA ref.

topic: Upstream plain S3 also violates part-before-Keeper
canonical_claim: Upstream plain S3 also violates part-before-Keeper durability on a process crash because blob data streams during write but local metadata, including tmp-to-final rename, remains queued until after the Keeper multi.

topic: PartWriteTxn::abandon can misreport a durably completed
canonical_claim: `PartWriteTxn::abandon` can misreport a durably completed operation if an unguarded `EventEmitter::emit` throws after `appendRefOps` succeeds.

topic: publishEntries can leak a durable live-epoch
canonical_claim: `publishEntries` can leak a durable live-epoch precommit when promote fails because its exception path does not call `abandon`, while the destructor only retires the build sequence and stale-precommit sweep and GC do not reclaim live precommits.

topic: MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts now commits every contract
canonical_claim: `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` now commits every part's disk-storage transaction before the Keeper commit decision, changing durability ordering for all `DiskObjectStorage`-backed MergeTree writes and requiring non-CA regression coverage before upstreaming. The required invariant is that a part is durable on its disk before its `block_id` and part-znode are registered in Keeper; parts-transaction commit only flips visibility, while rollback compensates with new operations over committed disk state. After `renameParts` returns, every part is durable at its final name; `Transaction::commit` only changes in-memory visibility, and rollback removes or compensates committed disk data. With the durability fix, a disk publish failure throws from `renameParts` before the Keeper multi, so no block-id znode exists and a retry inserts honestly. A crash between the Keeper multi and the later parts-transaction commit leaves the part durable at its final name, with a CA ref in the pool, so restart can see the part. If a later failure occurs after `renameParts`, rollback removes all preactive parts; published CA parts are reclaimed by ref removal and unpublished parts by temporary cleanup and destructor abandon, before any Keeper multi is reached. All audited `renameParts` call sites execute before an external commit decision or immediately before `commit` with no intervening decision, and paths bypassing it were found not to violate the durability invariant. The implementation closes each active part transaction in `renameParts` after deferred `renameTo`, while borrowed projection sub-parts do not independently commit because they share the parent's transaction. The generic durability invariant is that a part must be durably published before its Keeper block ID is registered; the proposed implementation closes the active disk transaction in `Transaction::renameParts` rather than adding CA-specific routing. The generic fix closes every part disk-storage transaction in `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` after deferred renames, with no CA-specific code change. The intended protocol is prepare durable and compensable storage before the Keeper decision, then apply visibility with a cheap finalize or compensate on abort; `renameParts` is the existing lock-free prepare slot. The agreed fix model closes the disk transaction at `renameParts`; a later parts-transaction commit has nothing left to do on disk, while rollback performs compensation as a new operation over committed state.

topic: A repoint path that abandons its
canonical_claim: A repoint path that abandons its scratch build must reset `st.build` after abandon or promote, because destructor re-abandonment raises `LOGICAL_ERROR` and can abort under `abort_on_logical_error` or ASan.

topic: The stage-1 fan-out originally scheduled a
canonical_claim: The stage-1 fan-out originally scheduled a task before appending its handle to an unreserved tracking vector, so a tracking allocation failure could leave a runnable task untracked and later dereferencing destroyed transaction or result-slot storage.

topic: If namespace birth publishes _ckpt and
canonical_claim: If namespace birth publishes `_ckpt` and then its ref-log `PUT` fails, the failed birth can leave durable `_ckpt` debris; the creation lifecycle must delete that `_ckpt` for a never-born namespace without deleting a live namespace's checkpoint.

topic: The existing ~PartWriteTxn unconditionally retires a
canonical_claim: The existing `~PartWriteTxn` unconditionally retires a build while an owner grant may be wedged-Unresolved, and staged-body cleanup can swallow failures until the epoch seals.

topic: removeDirectory, removeRecursive, and committed moveDirectory mutate
canonical_claim: `removeDirectory`, `removeRecursive`, and committed `moveDirectory` mutate durable refs immediately rather than through a rollback-capable transaction overlay, so aborting can leave durable refs changed and can publish a supposedly removed part.

topic: truncateFile reports success without changing bytes
canonical_claim: `truncateFile` reports success without changing bytes, so callers can observe successful truncation while old content remains.

topic: removeFile discards the if_exists flags and
canonical_claim: `removeFile` discards the `if_exists` flags and succeeds when a file is missing even for the non-`ifExists` API instead of throwing `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.

topic: Retrying a failed commit can report
canonical_claim: Retrying a failed commit can report success with refs absent because rollback removes published refs but leaves staging entries marked `published`, causing retry to skip them.

topic: Rename treats an unrelated existing destination
canonical_claim: Rename treats an unrelated existing destination as successful replay when the source is absent, even though no operation ID or content proof exists.

topic: Part-write construction failure can permanently pin
canonical_claim: Part-write construction failure can permanently pin the active-build watermark because the active sequence is inserted before `PartWriteTxn` construction and no destructor retires it after allocation or event-sink failure.

topic: Moving a part to a content_addressed
canonical_claim: Moving a part to a `content_addressed` disk through `ALTER TABLE ... MOVE PART ... TO DISK 'ca'` used `promote` for the `moving` ref and failed the unique-ref invariant when `moving` already named another manifest.

topic: Since TXN-ONE-PIPELINE Task 1.1, B151 CA
canonical_claim: Since TXN-ONE-PIPELINE Task 1.1, B151 CA durable publish operations ran inside MergeTreeData::Transaction::commit while holding the data_parts lock, causing concurrent queries needing that lock to stall behind S3 round trips.; Moving CA disk commit from `Transaction::commit` to `renameParts` moves S3 publish I/O off the `data_parts` lock without changing total I/O volume; the accepted cost is redo work when a later external decision rejects the part.
